_about: Language-agnostic behavioural test vectors for nhs-number, frozen against the Python reference implementation. Validated by tests/test_vectors.py, and intended to be consumed by implementations in other languages so they agree on what 'correct' means. 'region' names map to the package's REGION_* constants; 'range' names to the RANGE_* constants.
_licence: MIT, like the rest of the project. You may use these vectors freely to build an NHS number implementation in any language, including commercially. Attribution is appreciated but not required. See https://ohtf.github.io/nhs-number-py/other-languages/
_not_covered: Deliberately excluded: (1) language-specific input robustness - Python's guarantee that None, lists, floats and arbitrary objects never raise is tested natively, since 'unparseable input' differs by language; (2) generate(), which is random - assert its properties instead (valid, in the requested region, synthetic range by default); (3) disguise() outputs, which come from a seeded PRNG and would require reimplementing CPython's Mersenne Twister bit-for-bit - assert its properties instead (deterministic per number+seed, output valid, NHS fakes from the synthetic range, CHI fakes carrying '99' at digits 7-8 and a different date of birth).

calculate_checksum.note: checksum 10 means no single check digit can match - any number with this identifier is invalid

standardise.note: leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed
mixed separators are not a supported format

is_valid.note: integer input is zero-padded then validated
0000000000 has a valid checksum; range membership is a separate concern
checksum-valid; range is not checked without for_region (issue #44)
Scotland CHI, month 13 - impossible date; checksum is valid, only the date rejects it
Scotland CHI, 01/01/20 - valid under the modulus 10 check only (mod 11 gives 0)
mod 10 check digit matches, but the number is in the England/Wales range, where only mod 11 applies
mod 10 check digit matches, but 01/13/20 is not a real date, so the CHI date-of-birth rule rejects it

is_valid_for_region.note: synthetic number, not in the Scotland range

calculate_checksum_mod10.note: CHI (Scotland) modulus 10 check digit; the modulus 11 calculation gives 0, so a full number with this check digit is valid under mod 10 only
the modulus 11 calculation also gives 7, so this identifier is valid under both
mod 10 matches, but this identifier is England/Wales range where only mod 11 applies
